preview: An internship interview experience at Citi for the ICG Tech role by Soham Ghadge, detailing the online assessment, technical round, and HR round.
content: INTERNSHIP INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE NAME BRANCH SOHAM GHADGE ELECTRONICS & TELECOMMUNICATION Eligibility Criteria CGPA: 6.5 Eligible Branches: CS, IT and Circuit branches Active Backlogs: No Dead Backlogs: Yes Stipend: INR 75,000 per month Role: Institutional Clients Group (ICG Tech) The entire process was divided in the following rounds: Online Test Round ( 1hr 30 minutes) Interview Rounds: 1) Technical Round ( 50minutes ) 2) HR Round ( 15 minutes ) PRE-PLACEMENT TALK This is the time where you understand about the company, its goals, its objectives and their work areas. It is a great time for you to ask any questions you have about the role, the process and anything you have in mind related to the upcoming internship process. It might seem like a waste of time to a few but it’s not. You can use the company’s language and values in your answers which could give you an upper hand in the interview process. . Duration : 1 hour ONLINE ASSESSMENT Duration : 1 hr 30 minutes The online assessment for each roles were different. Since I had ICG Tech role as my 1st preference, I had the following format - Coding Section (45 minutes - 2 questions) SQL ( 15 minutes - 12 MCQs) React ( 15 minutes - 12 MCQs) Angular ( 15 minutes - 12 MCQs) Coding Section - I didn't expect this section to go so smoothly, as I received questions from the previous year, which I had luckily practiced beforehand . This preparation gave me an advantage. It's worth mentioning that learning from your seniors' interview experiences can be invaluable, so please take the time to go through them. The questions asked to me were as follows - Question 1: A stock trader deals in N stocks and calculates their relative price changes. The trader's lucky number is K, so they want to invest in the stock with the Kth smallest relative price. Write an algorithm to find the Kth smallest stock price from the list of N stocks. Solution Logic: Sort the list of stock prices in ascending order and return the Kth smallest value by accessing the (K-1) index in the sorted list. This section included 12 multiple-choice questions on SQL, with topics ranging from basic queries to DDL, DML, TCL commands, and aggregate functions. SQL being my strongest domain, I found this section very manageable. SQL - Question: You are given N flowers and their stem lengths. Arrange the first K flowers in increasing order of stem length, and the remaining (N-K) flowers in decreasing order. Solution Logic: Sort the first K flowers in ascending order and the remaining (N-K) flowers in descending order. Use the sort function twice, with the second sort using a comparator (greater<int>()) for descending order. React - This section included 12 multiple-choice questions on React, focusing on key concepts such as React lifecycle methods, types of components, and code snippets with missing terms. This section was of medium difficulty. Angular - I wasn't fully prepared for this section, but after reading about it in my senior's interview experiences, I decided to prepare for it the day before the OA. The section ranged from medium to hard difficulty. For the questions I wasn't sure about, I selected random options since there was no negative marking. INTERVIEW The interview was scheduled online on October 4th and conducted via Zoom. Out of 200 registered participants, only 40 students were shortlisted for interviews—28 for the ICG role and 12 for the PBWM role. My interview was set for 11:30 AM but was delayed by an hour. For the ICG tech role, there were only two rounds: one technical and one HR. I joined the interview at 12:30 PM sharp and started with a warm greeting. The interviewer kicked off by asking me to introduce myself. This is a typical question, and it's important to prepare for it in advance. I made sure my introduction was impactful, steering the conversation toward databases, which is my strongest area. Databases: I was asked to compare NoSQL (MongoDB) and SQL databases. I explained their differences in depth, I also mentioned about horizontal and vertical scaling which led to another deep discussion about the scaling methods! This helped me to get a strong start with the interview! Then he asked me why I often choose MongoDB for my projects, to which I emphasized on its flexibility and performance with complex queries. The interviewer also asked about the concept of a document in MongoDB and how it contrasts with a row in SQL, and I explained the structural differences. DSA : Next, I faced a problem involving an n x n x n 3D array. The task was to find occurrences of a specific word or string within the array. I started with a brute-force solution. He then asked me to optimise it to which I asked for a hint. However, the interviewer realized the question wasn’t framed correctly and shifted focus to Git, where I admitted I wasn’t as confident. He appreciated the honesty and moved on. Web Dev : He asked with about which frontend and backend technologies I had worked in, to which I replied MERN Stack! He then asked me where majorly I had contributed in the project. I told him that I was majorly involved in the backend side of it like JWT Auth and Database management. We then entered to discuss about JWT auth process in depth and what all error codes we faced during authentication. I was asked about the common error codes that might arise during authentication processes, particularly: 401 (Unauthorized), 402 (Payment Required), 403 (Forbidden), 404 (Not Found) and 501 (Internal Server Error). I was surprised as I didnt expect this to be asked although I was familiar with 401 and 404, I told him that I didnt know about 402, 403 and 501. He then told me about 501 ! TECHNICAL ROUND (50 minutes) Additionally, I was asked to give a wild guess about the difference between 401 and 501 , where I clarified that 401 indicates an authentication failure, while 501 refers to the server's inability to recognize the request method. Boom this is how I ended up with Web Dev! That was a good grilling session! Computer Networks (CCN) : The interviewer tested my knowledge of computer networks since I belong to EXTC, particularly in the context of the Application Layer protocol. He wanted me to explain the differences between HTTP and HTTPS. I explained that HTTPS adds a layer of encryption (via SSL/TLS), making it more secure compared to HTTP, which transmits data in plaintext. Luckily I had this in my sem at the moment and had given a MST on it , indeed I answered this very well! Conclusion : At the end, the interviewer asked if I had any questions for him. I used this opportunity to ask about his career journey and his current role in the company. This led to a meaningful 6-7 minute conversation, which gave me deeper insight into his experience and the company’s work culture. Key Takeaways Throughout the interview, I stayed confident in the areas I was strong in, like databases and web dev. When asked about Git, I was upfront about my lack of confidence, and that honesty was appreciated. It’s crucial not to bluff—if you don’t know something, just say so. This builds trust and reflects well on your integrity. My interview concluded at 12:55 PM, after which I had lunch while anxiously waiting for the results. By 1:45 PM, the results were out, and thankfully, I was selected for the next round—the HR round. Out of all the candidates, only 9 students were shortlisted for this round for my role. I felt confident heading into the HR round, knowing that my strong communication skills and ability to connect with people would serve me well. TECHNICAL ROUND (50 minutes) HR ROUND (15 minutes) My HR round was scheduled for 2:45 PM, and it followed the usual format of HR interviews. I was asked to introduce myself, talk about my hobbies, family background, and whether I’d be open to relocating to Pune. The interviewer also inquired about my future plans and why I chose Citi as my potential employer. The conversation then shifted to Citi's three leadership principles. I was asked how I align with them, to which I provided examples from my experience managing Ecell’s flagship event, UNICUS, demonstrating leadership and organizational skills. The interviewer also covered a few standard questions like whether I knew anyone already working at Citi or if I had any connections with government employees. I made sure to end the interview on a strong note with a closing statement, reaffirming my interest in the role, and asked a few thoughtful questions about Citi and its work culture. Conclusion - At around 8.30, we got the result and about 10 people were selected for the internship (7 for ICG role and 3 for PBWM role) and I was proud to be one of them! TECHNICAL ROUND (50 minutes) Preparation Tips 1.Choose a DSA Sheet: Follow any DSA sheet that suits you—Striver, Arsh Goyal, Love Babbar, or Neetcode 75. I personally found Striver Sheet better. Focus on understanding the concepts, no matter where you practice from. Striver_SDE_Sheet 2. Fundamentals: For core subjects like OS, DBMS, and CN, any YouTube playlist will work. If you've studied them well in your course, a quick revision a day before the interview will suffice. 3. Be Ready for Common Questions: Frame your responses to basic questions like "Tell me about yourself," "What are your strengths and weaknesses," and "Where do you see yourself in the next few years?" Answer confidently, and use the STAR method for situation-based questions. 4. Study Interview Experiences: Read as many interview experiences as you can—GFG, Glassdoor, this drive,etc. Sometimes, you might encounter the same questions in your own interview, boosting your confidence . 5. Know Your Resume: Be well-versed with the projects listed on your resume. Whether it was a team effort or individual work, you should be able to explain the flow and rationale behind your choices confidently. 6. Stay Resilient: Interviewing can be stressful, and rejections can affect your confidence. However, every failed interview is a step closer to success. Learn from each experience, and remember that factors like luck also play a role. 7. Be Honest and Authentic: Don’t embellish your resume or bluff your way through questions. Interviewers can tell when you’re being dishonest, so always speak about what you know. 8. Get Support: Talk to trusted seniors or friends. They can offer guidance, share experiences, and help you navigate the process. You're not alone in this journey . 9. Practice Your Introduction: Practicing how you introduce yourself is important, especially to avoid forgetting key details. Try rehearsing in front of a mirror to build confidence . TECHNICAL ROUND (50 minutes) 10. Research the Company: Learn about the company’s mission, culture, and principles before your interview. Always have thoughtful questions ready to ask the interviewer, as it shows genuine interest. Remember to stay calm, trust the process, and give it your all! Good luck! :) Want to connect with me?
